newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK offsets falling prices, leaves BUX flat.
newsitem.headline: TVK offsets falling prices, leaves BUX flat.

text.p: Chemicals stock TVK stole the show on Tuesday, offsetting falls in other leading stocks which weakened due to the expiry of June BUX futures, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,313.18 points, down 13.94.

TVK leapt almost three percent by the end of play to finish at 2,995 forints, up 85, bolstered by market talk about the imminent payout of five billion forints plus an additional one billion accumulated interest by privatisation agency APV.
TVK is expected to cash in five billion forints and an additional one billion of accumulated interest under the provisions of Hungary's previous privatisation law.
APV declined to comment on the rumours.

"TVK's was the day favourite, reached 3,000 forints once again, and had strong turnover," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment. "Talk of APV's five billion forints revived again and this gave a boost to TVK."

TVK's rise mostly cancelled out falls in other leading stocks, including OTP Bank, meat processor Pick and pharmaceuticals Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt which fell as investors sold them due to the expiry day of June BUX futures.

"The expiry day of June BUX futures explained falls in shares like (pharmaceuticals) Richter, OTP, Pick, as investors sold these papers," Cselovszki said, adding these stocks might recover on Wednesday.
Elsewhere on the market, chemicals BorsodChem added 60 forints to end at 7,105, with its turnover boosted by an agency cross for 150,000 shares at 7,150 forints.
OTP closed at 4,450 forints, down 50; Pick at 13,200 forints, down 300, and Egis at 11,500 forints, down 300.
Cselovszki expected some corrections of three to five percent to come in the near future.
Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London, said a slower period was likely in the coming month with little news to trade on.
"This will be when Poland absorbs slightly above one billion dollars and when no major (Hungarian) corporate news is likely," Sitanyi said.
He was referring to offerings of shares in copper concern KGHM Polska and in Bank Handlowy of Poland.
